clue.text: China's not developed support

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is taken as the letters of China plus S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that China's economy has failed to build up its backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges CHINAS and NOT; the apostrophe's S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar used to prop something up, a structural support.

clue.text: "Sir" as heard in Bangalore primarily?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of each word in the run before it

explanation.surface: A question about how the respectful term of address sounds in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the initial letters of Sir, as, heard, in, Bangalore; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India the Hindi-Urdu title was the respectful form of address used for a man, equivalent to sir or master.

clue.text: Prepared to meet their death, ignoring one with lots of weapons

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a fresh arrangement
ignoring tells us one letter of the run is left out of the rearrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Soldiers braced to die, with someone excused from the heavily armed group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges TO MEET THEIR DEATH, and 'ignoring' drops one I (one) from those sixteen letters, leaving fifteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone carrying every weapon they could possibly need, so heavily armed.

clue.text: Memorise old lines to speak

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
verse is poetry, written in lines

explanation.surface: An actor told to learn some ancient lines in order to deliver them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' flags that CON in the sense of memorise is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk with someone, so it is a synonym for speaking.

clue.text: Jot a letter

definitions.meaning: a jot is a tiny amount, as in not one jot
a character of the Greek alphabet, its ninth

explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter gave its name to the idea of a minute quantity, just like a jot.

clue.text: Boldness to lie on impulse may rely on this for delivery

definitions.text: impulse may rely on this for delivery

parts.note: nerve means daring or boldness
a fib is a small lie
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A brazen fibber depends on an impulse to deliver their story.
explanation.walkthrough: The impulse is a nerve signal, not a whim; RE means 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical impulses in the body are carried along these strands of nervous tissue.

clue.text: Part of time signal edited and transmitted by wire

parts.note: the broadcast time signal is a series of short pips, each one a pip

explanation.surface: A radio time signal partly cut and then sent down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The time signal on BBC radio is six short beeps called the pips.
explanation.definitionFit: Music or sound that is piped is carried along cables or wires to where it is heard.

clue.text: Gaunt from illness that's reached a maximum level

definitions.meaning: looking pale and drawn after being ill
having hit its high point, as a price that has topped out

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pinched and sickly-looking, while the verb's past form means having hit a summit.

clue.text: Among coppers, toss coin: heads may be a curse in disguise

indicators.note: among puts the scrambled letters inside the word for the police

parts.note: coppers is slang for police officers

indicators.note: toss means the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers flip a coin, though calling heads may bring bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss' rearranges the coin and heads letters; 'Among' sets them inside the police. Coppers are policemen here, not pennies, and 'may be' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an apparent prize or honour that turns out to bring harm, a curse that looks like a blessing.

clue.text: Wordless cast are astounding

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A silent troupe of actors gives an amazing performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company; it is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to amaze, so 'they dumbfound' replaces 'they are astounding'.

clue.text: After soft sound, girl crumpled in arms: I will show concern for welfare

indicators.note: after says the rest of the word follows the opening sound

parts.note: a hum is a low gentle sound
Anita is a girl's name

indicators.note: crumpled means squashed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl murmurs and collapses into someone's embrace, promising to care for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges ANITA, IN, ARMS and I; 'will show' only links the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanitarianism is the belief in promoting human welfare and caring for people in need.

clue.text: Harry who pins an emblem on?

definitions.meaning: to harry is to pester or harass persistently
a whimsical reading: someone who fixes a badge to a lapel

explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester repeatedly, like harry; the second sense jokingly takes the word as one who badges.

clue.text: Wife was blooming nearly getting over man going wild occasionally

indicators.note: getting over means the shortened word is turned around, read in the opposite direction
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: was blooming means flowered

explanation.surface: A wife flourished almost as she recovered from a man who sometimes ran riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was blooming' is a past-tense verb phrase, flowered; 'nearly' trims its last letter and 'getting over' turns the remainder round after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore's shape-shifter is a human who turns into a savage wolf from time to time, at full moon.

clue.text: Magazine from soldier on view

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
an eye is a view or way of seeing something

explanation.surface: A periodical taken from a soldier on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a long-running British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye is the name of a well-known British satirical and current affairs magazine.

clue.text: One way to produce artist's channel in New Zealand

parts.note: reading cook as a signal to rearrange, cooking the letters of strait gives artist

explanation.surface: A method for creating an artist's sea passage in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Cook Strait separates New Zealand's North and South Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The strait is the stretch of sea dividing New Zealand's two main islands, named after Captain Cook.

clue.text: Original theory scattered gloom with convenient binding

indicators.note: binding means the outer word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: cosy can mean comfortable and convenient, as in a cosy arrangement

indicators.note: scattered means the letters are spread into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new idea dispersed despair with a comfortable book cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges gloom and 'binding' wraps the comfortable word round it, as a book's cover binds pages. The definition is about the origin of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmology studies the origin and development of the universe, a theory of how everything began.

clue.text: Trixie meets posh boyfriend

parts.note: Trixie and Bea are both pet forms of Beatrix
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A girl named Trixie is introduced to a wealthy suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Trixie is a pet name for Beatrix, as is Bea.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a male admirer or sweetheart, an old-fashioned term for a lover.

clue.text: What could be better than cheap summer skydiving practice?

definitions.text: What could be better than cheap summer
definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: an autumn costing nothing beats a low-priced summer
the part of a jump before the parachute opens

explanation.definitionFit: In the US 'fall' is autumn, so a free fall could be read as a costless autumn; it is also unchecked descent in skydiving.

clue.text: London area told to plant seeds and dig up weeds?

indicators.note: told signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.words: to plant seeds and dig up weeds
parts.note: to plant seeds is to sow, and to dig up weeds is to hoe

explanation.surface: A London district is advised to take up some gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a lively district of central London famous for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Finished and paid, having eaten cereal that's not worth the cost

parts.note: over means finished or ended

indicators.note: having eaten means the abbreviation swallows the grain

parts.note: pd is the abbreviation for paid
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A diner finished, settled the bill and grumbled that the cereal was a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having eaten' puts the cereal inside the abbreviation for paid; 'that's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs more than it is worth, so it is poor value.

clue.text: Upset old Indonesian islander's native people

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a Javan is a native of Java, an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Java is distressed about his community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' in a down clue reads the islander backwards, before the abbreviation for old. Java is an island of Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Person driven from class, almost expelled, having turned 20 in it

indicators.note: in it means the turned piece goes inside the shortened word
almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: ousted means expelled

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 20 across means function, and so does act

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out of their group, nearly banished, after turning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the word for expelled; 'turned' reverses act, which is what 20 (BEHAVE) means; 'in it' puts that inside. 'having' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcaste is someone expelled from their caste in Hindu society, losing their social class.

clue.text: Extremely bothersome to hold function

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: to have is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: Something very irritating is required to hold an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes B and E, the two ends of bothersome.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that behaves works properly, so to behave can mean to function.

clue.text: Alien skirting Germany's borders, parking in another country

indicators.note: skirting means going around the edges, so the alien encloses the other letters

parts.note: ET is the film alien

indicators.note: borders means only the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A space creature travels around Germany's frontiers to park elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' gives GY from Germany; 'skirting' wraps E...T round GY plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country of north-east Africa, a nation distinct from Germany.

clue.text: Knight getting time in prison

indicators.note: getting means the title takes in a letter, receiving it within

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A knight is sentenced to a term in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is informal slang for a jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Group allowing no sharing of responsibility for issue?

definitions.text: Group allowing no sharing of responsibility for issue?

parts.words: Group allowing no sharing of responsibility for issue?
parts.note: issue means children, and the household described has a single adult raising them alone

explanation.definitionFit: A household where one mother or father brings up the children without a partner to share the load.

clue.text: Many a hoodlum harbours this brute

indicators.note: harbours means the words hold the answer concealed within them

explanation.surface: A crowd of thugs shelters a savage among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbours' points to the letters running across manY A HOOdlum.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, named after the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Liberal soldiers in small measure decline signing up

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure, half an em

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for decline

parts.note: rot means decay or decline
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A Liberal army in decline after taking only a little care with recruitment.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a small typesetting width. 'in' sets the Liberal soldiers inside the word for decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of registering or joining up, as for a course or the forces.
